subject: Post-call recap: token economics checklist + overage playbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: token economics checklist + overage playbook

Alex — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get you a clean proposal and launch path. TL;DR: please confirm the daily peak window size and approved budget range so we can size a temporary quota bump or prepay option.

Recap of what you shared (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Expected steady-state: ~8M tokens / month (model: redwood-compat-xxl) for your scheduled reports and background inference.
- Launch / marketing spikes: short, concentrated bursts during re-report runs — you estimated up to ~100M additional tokens over 1 week for a product launch; typical micro-bursts ~500k–1.2M tokens within a 5-minute window during peak usage.
- Target unit economics: you're looking to land somewhere between $1,200–$1,800 per 1M tokens for initial pricing (goal is predictable cost during launch).

Redwood recommended guardrails and pricing options (first pass):
1) Committed baseline (monthly): 8M tokens @ $1,500 / 1M tokens.
2) Burst allowance: up to 10% of monthly commit available as short-term burst capacity without immediate overage billing, applied as a rolling 24-hour pool (i.e., up to 800k tokens can be used as burst credit per rolling day).
3) Temporary launch uplift: for one-off launch windows, we can provision a time-limited quota bump (validated by a signed amendment or prepayment). Example: 100M extra tokens over 7 days would be priced at the committed rate if prepaid; otherwise standard overage applies.
4) Overage pricing: $2,200 / 1M tokens for non-committed usage beyond burst allowance (applies in the billing period).
5) Approval flow for quota increases: engineering request -> AE approval -> ops implement; for >50% uplifts we require 24–48h lead time for scheduling.

Next steps / asks for you: please confirm the following so we can produce a one-page SOW + amendment:
- Finalized monthly commit target (confirm 8M or provide updated #).
- Maximum anticipated single-window burst (tokens in a 5-minute window).
- Budget range for initial 3 months (so we can model prepay vs overage).

Attachments: I’m attaching our token economics playbook and a simple launch example workbook so you can see the math. (redwood_token_econ_playbook.pdf, finlytics_launch_example.xlsx)

If you want, we can run a quick 20-minute follow-up tomorrow to walk through the workbook and pick a route (prepay vs temporary bump vs pure overage).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment stubs: redwood_token_econ_playbook.pdf (12 pages), finlytics_launch_example.xlsx (workbook, 2 sheets)

From: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@finlytics.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 17:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token economics checklist + overage playbook

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Baseline: we’re comfortable confirming 8M tokens/month to start.
- Peak: the 100M is a one-week figure for launch (spread over several big jobs). The worst single observed micro-burst from our staging tests was ~1.1M tokens in a 5-minute window (that’s the metric I care about most).
- Budget: we have a launch budget in the $120k–$180k range for the first month including hosting and inference. If your math shows we’ll be inside there for a prepaid path, we’d prefer that for predictability.

Two asks:
1) Can you give a worked example of the cost for a 7-day launch that consumes an extra 100M tokens (I care about prepay vs overage math).
2) Will Redwood allow a one-time temporary quota bump for launch without requiring a full commit (i.e., we pay overage to avoid long-term commit but want guaranteed capacity)?

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow afternoon.

—Alex
Alex Jordan
Head of Product | Finlytics
alex.jordan@finlytics.io | +1 (213) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@finlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token economics checklist + overage playbook

Alex — appreciate the detail. Attached workbook has two scenarios; below is the shorthand math so you can see the spread quickly.

Scenario A — Prepay (recommended for predictability):
- Extra launch consumption: 100M tokens.
- Prepay price assumption (committed rate): $1,500 / 1M tokens.
- Cost = 100 * $1,500 = $150,000 (one-time, applied to month of launch).
- Benefit: no overage surcharge and we reserve capacity; qualifies you for preferred scheduling and lower lead time.

Scenario B — Overage (no extra commit):
- Overage rate: $2,200 / 1M tokens.
- Cost = 100 * $2,200 = $220,000 (one-time overage bill).
- Benefit: no long-term commitment; downside = higher price and no guaranteed reserved slots — we still try to accommodate bursts but cannot guarantee dedicated capacity without an amendment.

Temporary quota bump option (middle ground):
- We can provision a one-week quota bump that keeps you on the overage billing plan but with a hard-guaranteed reserve for the agreed window.
- Pricing model: overage rate with a small reservation fee (example: $8k reservation fee for the week + overage at $2,200/1M for any consumption beyond reserved amount).
- Operationally: requires signed amendment at least 48 hours before the uplift window for a >50% increase in quota. Smaller uplifts (<50%) can often be done with 24h notice.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) If you want predictability, confirm prepay (we’ll draft amendment to apply to September bill).
2) If you prefer flexibility, confirm the exact 7-day window and we’ll run an ops check and quote the reservation fee + uplift amount.

I’ve cc’d Marissa (Customer Success) to draft a brief runbook for rate-limit configuration and Dev (my manager) to sign off on a one-time credit if we decide to provide a launch credit.

I’ll hold a 20-minute slot tomorrow at 13:30 PT; please confirm if that works.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token economics checklist + overage playbook

Looping internally to confirm approvals — a couple of notes from ops/finance side:
- We can approve a modest, one-time launch credit up to $15,000 for new mid-market customers where it materially reduces ramp friction. Higher credits require RevOps approval.
- For a 100M token launch, the prepay path is the cleanest from an operational perspective and avoids the complexity of temporary reservations. If they prepay, ops will reserve capacity.
- Please have Marissa prepare a short runbook that includes:
  - exact rate-limit bucket values to apply (tokens/min and TTL for KV caches),
  - a rollback policy if latencies increase during the launch, and
  - the on-call escalation list for the 7-day window.

Marissa — can you draft that runbook and share it to the Drive link below? I’ll coordinate with Finance on whether we can stretch to a larger goodwill credit if this closes quickly.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-token-econ

Thanks —
